title: Dynamic residency curves and batch shaping for variant-specific long-context tuning
creator: Marcus Li
description: Spike + implementation ticket to design and roll out a per-variant residency-curve system that shapes KV cache residency and batch formation heuristics for long-context variants (Llama, Mistral, Qwen). The goal is to reduce peak GPU memory pressure and tail latency regressions when we enable aggressive continuous batching on long-context configs. This is a follow-up to earlier memory-profile work but focuses on dynamic residency curves (soft eviction thresholds over time) and batch shaping (prefetch windows + batch size caps per model variant).
acceptance_criteria: Per-variant residency curves implemented and configurable via model profile
End-to-end tests validating eviction correctness under synthetic long-sequence workloads
Memory peak reduction >= 12% on average across evaluated long-context variants (measured on rtx-a6000 baseline) OR no increase in OOM incidents during 48h soak
No more than 5% regression in p50 latency and no more than 10% regression in p99 during continuous batching under production-like QPS
Rollout plan with canary gating in console and automated rollback on memory/latency regression alerts
Documentation in RFC + runtime config docs and a demo dashboard in the Console showing residency curves and batch composition
implementation_plan: Spike: microbench per-variant residency curves using synthetic prompts (1 week)
Design: residency curve schema + config knobs (soft_threshold_pct, warm_period_tokens, decay_tau, batch_shaping_window) (3 days)
Runtime: integrate residency controller into KV manager and batching router (2 weeks)
Tests: unit + integration + soak on dedicated nodes (3 days)
Rollout: staged canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full with automated metric checks (1 week)
Postmortem + tuning pass after 72h full rollout
notes: Motivation: previous static memory profiles cause suboptimal eviction timing for models with bursty long-token usages (e.g., multi-turn chat with long context). If we let continuous batching run without model-aware residency shaping, KV cache balloons then triggers expensive evictions/allocations that spike p99 latencies.

Key idea: treat KV residency as a curve over token time instead of a single footprint number. Residency curve maps token-age -> keep_probability. Combine with batch shaping window so that requests likely to reuse KV stay resident while low-reuse prefixes are soft-evicted earlier.

We observed in the spike that a simple exponential decay residency curve reduced transient GPU memory by ~18% for llama-2-13b-longctx under synthetic document ingestion; Mistral-7B-longctx saw ~11% and Qwen-7B-longctx ~9%. These numbers are preliminary and sensitive to batching policy.

Tradeoffs considered: more aggressive decay improves memory but increases reheating (cache re-population) cost which impacts p99. We plan to expose decay_tau per-variant and an adaptive reheating limiter tied to observed reaccess rate.

Fallback: if residency controller detects >8% p99 increase and >5% memory churn, automatically fall back to the model's baseline static profile and disable continuous batching for that variant during the canary window.
Related work: links to earlier memory profile tickets and slab allocator experiments (dependencies listed).
updates: 2026-02-18: Ticket created by Marcus Li. Initial triage and scope agreed with PM + infra. Assigned to Elena Park.

2026-02-22: Spike started. Completed synthetic harness for measuring token-age reuse and peak resident set. Harness available at https://github.com/redwood-inference/kvc-spike/tree/feature/residency-curves

2026-02-27: Spike results: exponential decay vs linear soft-threshold - exponential decay had better steady-state memory under continuous batching for Llama variants. Draft results uploaded: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1ResCurveSpike

2026-03-03: Design review with runtime and batching owners. Agreed on residency schema: {soft_threshold_pct, warm_period_tokens, decay_tau, min_keep_prob} and batch_shaping_window param. Action: Elena to prototype KV controller integration.

2026-03-07: Prototype KV controller implemented on feature branch and validated on a single rtx-a6000 node. Observed memory peak reduction ~15% for llama-2-13b-longctx at continuous batching QPS=20. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1248

2026-03-09: Integration tests failing intermittently under mixed-variant workload (reheating thrash). Added reheating limiter and per-variant reheating counters. Discovered a bug in batch router where long-prefix grouping disabled windowing for Qwen variants; patch in progress.
Next: stabilize tests, add canary rollout config in Console, write docs and dashboard panels for residency curve visibility (owner: Elena)
